calibration.desc.temperature: Prints a tower with blocks at different temperatures and judges which gives the best result (less stringing, better layer adhesion, cleaner overhangs). Record the temperature of the winning block.
calibration.desc.pressureAdvance: Compensates the pressure lag when speed changes, to avoid over/under-extrusion on corners and edges. A single fixed value for all print conditions.
calibration.desc.adaptivePa: Like Pressure Advance, but the best value changes with speed, flow and acceleration. Record one point (PA + flow + acceleration) per run; add several to build the table.
calibration.desc.flowRatio: Finds the right amount of extrusion for a consistent surface and accurate dimensions, avoiding gaps (under-extrusion) or rough surfaces (over-extrusion).
calibration.desc.tolerance: Checks the dimensional accuracy of printer + filament by printing hexagonal holes with different offsets (0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 mm) and measuring them with calipers. Record the offset that fit best.
calibration.desc.vfa: Finds the speed range that causes resonance artifacts (visible ripples) on vertical walls, so the slicer can avoid those speeds.
calibration.desc.volumetricSpeed: Finds the maximum flow (mm³/s) your printer + filament can handle without defects or jams, so the hotend is not asked for more than it can melt.
calibration.desc.ironing: A second pass over top surfaces with very low flow to smooth them. OrcaSlicer has no dedicated calibration wizard for this; flow and speed are tuned by trial and error.

matdef.help.mvs: How much material the nozzle can melt and extrude per second without losing quality. It usually limits real print speed more than the speed in mm/s.
matdef.help.flowRatio: Correction factor for the extrusion flow relative to the slicer's reference value, to compensate for how this particular filament behaves.
matdef.help.tensileXY: Maximum force the material resists when stretched before breaking (ASTM D638). XY = in the print plane.
matdef.help.tensileZ: Same as Tensile XY but measured between layers (Z axis); usually the weakest point of a 3D-printed part.
matdef.help.flexXY: Maximum force the part resists when bent before yielding or breaking (ASTM D790).
matdef.help.flexZ: Flexural strength (ASTM D790) measured between layers (Z axis).
matdef.help.elongXY: How far the material stretches before breaking, as a % of its original length (ASTM D638). Higher = more flexible/ductile.
matdef.help.elongZ: Elongation at break (ASTM D638) measured between layers (Z axis).
matdef.help.izod: Energy a notched sample absorbs before breaking from an impact (Izod, ASTM D256). Higher = more impact resistant.
matdef.help.charpy: Energy the material absorbs from an impact in a 3-point support test (Charpy, ISO 179). Measures toughness, similar to Izod.
matdef.help.softening: Temperature above which the material starts losing stiffness and deforms under its own weight or a light load.
matdef.help.vicat: Temperature at which a standard needle penetrates 1 mm into the material under load (ASTM D1525 / ISO 306). Measures heat resistance under point pressure.
matdef.help.tg: Glass transition temperature: above it the material goes from a rigid/brittle state to a soft, flexible one.
matdef.help.melting: Temperature at which the material goes from solid to liquid. Only applies to semi-crystalline materials (PLA, PETG, Nylon...).
matdef.help.mfr: Grams of material that flow through a standard orifice in 10 min under a defined temperature and weight (ASTM D1238). High = flows easily; low = more viscous.
matdef.help.shore: Resistance of the material to an indenter penetrating its surface (ASTM D2240). Most relevant for flexible filaments such as TPU.
matdef.help.ams: Automatic filament-change systems (Bambu Lab AMS and variants) this material is compatible with, according to the manufacturer.
matdef.help.plates: Build surfaces the manufacturer recommends for good adhesion with this material.

spool.fieldsHelp.location: Where you physically keep this spool — a shelf, a drawer, a dry box, or the printer it is loaded in. Spools are grouped by location in your library, so it is how you find one again.

spool.fieldsHelp.spoolWeight: What this spool weighs when empty. Leave it blank to follow the filament's spool weight, and set it when this particular spool differs — a respooled roll, or a cardboard core swapped for a plastic one. It is what gets subtracted from the reading when you adjust by measured weight, so a wrong one misstates how much filament is left.
spool.fieldsHelp.usedWeight: How much filament has been used from the spool. A new spool should have 0g used.
spool.fieldsHelp.weight: How much filament this spool held when full (net weight, not counting the spool itself). Leave it blank to follow the filament's weight, and set it when this particular spool differs — a partial roll, or the same filament bought on a larger one.
